yourBench.eyebrow: Your traffic · both sides metered by your provider
yourBench.title: Your own bench
yourBench.intro: The published bench runs our scenarios. This one runs yours: with verification sampling on, a random share of your eligible requests is also sent unoptimized to your own provider, and each pair is metered on both sides.
yourBench.offBody: Nothing has been checked in this window. Add the setting below to createSavingsLayer and your pairs will start to appear here.
yourBench.offCost: Each check is a real call to your provider, paid by you: roughly the sampling rate times what that traffic would cost without the layer. It never enters your statement or any commission.
yourBench.collectingBody: Below {min} pairs an interval would say more than the data. The counts below are already final.
yourBench.collectingGroupsTitle: Collecting pairs: {n} so far, but some groups are still short
yourBench.collectingGroupsBody: Groups with fewer than {min} pairs still make up {gap} of your eligible requests. A headline without enough pairs from them could hide the traffic where the layer costs you money, so it appears once they are {max} or less. The counts below are already final.
yourBench.readFailed: Could not read your pairs just now. Nothing below is a zero: try again in a moment.
yourBench.notAvailable: Your bench is not available on this server yet.
yourBench.headlineCaption: estimated from {pairs} pairs compared: the lower bound of the {level} interval for your eligible requests. Point estimate {point}, upper {upper} — we headline the floor.
yourBench.headlineCaptionPartial: estimated from {pairs} pairs compared: the lower bound of the {level} interval for the {coverage} of your eligible requests in groups that have pairs; the rest are not in this figure. Point estimate {point}, upper {upper} — we headline the floor.
yourBench.meanDiff: Mean difference per {per} requests: {point} (from {lower} to {upper}, {level} interval).
yourBench.basis: {pairs} pairs compared · they cover {coverage} of your {eligible} eligible requests · {rate} of those requests came back as a pair
yourBench.subsampled: Computed on a random subset of {n} of your {total} pairs.
yourBench.stressBody: Your unoptimized copies are sent only now and then, so they rarely find your provider's cache warm; without the layer, every request would. Priced as if every input token of each copy had been read from cache — at the cached-input rate of the price table, or free when it has none — the lower bound is {lower}.
yourBench.costBody: {usd} for {pairs} unoptimized copies, at the price table's rates. This is the cost of the instrument; it never enters your statement or any commission.
yourBench.costUnknown: Plus {n} copies whose cost could not be measured: no usage counter, closed while running, or failed or timed out. Your provider may still have billed some of them.
yourBench.strataTitle: By how the layer served the request
yourBench.notCovered: Too few pairs for an interval of its own ({n} of {min})
yourBench.naiveQuality: Pairs not compared, because the unoptimized copy did not finish the way your requests must to be checked — cut off by the output limit: {truncated} · stopped for another reason: {incomplete} · missed your output contract: {missed}. They are counted and in the CSV, but left out of every figure: a pair counts only when both sides finished normally.
yourBench.exclusionsIntro: These requests are counted but never sent twice: comparing them would not be comparing like with like. Fail-open, cut-off and failed-contract requests are often the layer's most expensive ones, so leaving them out can flatter the figure; that is why each one is shown here.
yourBench.exclusionsNone: No request was excluded in this window.

excluded.fail_open: Took the fail-open path (sent without optimizing)
excluded.truncated: Cut off by the output limit
excluded.contract_failed: Did not meet their output contract
excluded.unmeasured: No usage counter from your provider
excluded.retrieval: The layer added retrieved documents: no like-for-like copy

yourBench.outcomesTitle: Checks that did not become pairs

outcome.check_failed: Your provider returned an error, or the copy timed out
outcome.check_unmeasured: Your provider returned no usage counter
outcome.abandoned: Still running when the layer was closed
outcome.dropped: Not sent: too many checks were already running

yourBench.methodBody: Each pair is one request: what the unoptimized copy cost and what the optimized request cost, both from your provider's usage counters at the price table's rates. A pair counts only when the copy finished normally and met your output contract, the same rule your own requests must pass to be checked. Requests are grouped by how the layer served them, and each group is weighted by its share of your eligible requests. The interval is a stratified percentile bootstrap: {resamples} resamples, seed {seed}. With the CSV and the counts on this page you can recompute every point estimate; your intervals will match ours within resampling noise.

caveats.sample: A random sample, not every request: the figures describe your eligible traffic with the uncertainty shown, and they are never turned into an amount to bill.
caveats.randomness: Two calls rarely answer alike unless you fix the seed and set temperature to zero. That widens the interval. A pair counts only when both sides finished normally, so an answer cut off on one side only is never counted as a saving.
caveats.outside: Costs outside your provider call, such as an embedding service you run yourself, are in neither side.
caveats.streaming: Requests that failed, or that you cancelled while streaming, are not counted.

installLicensePanel.heading: Three steps. Your prompts never touch our servers.
installLicensePanel.step1: 1 · Get your license key — the SDK is public but fail-closed; it only runs with a valid key. Passed as licenseKey.
installLicensePanel.step2: 2 · Create & verify a service-account key — a machine credential (bvk_…) that does two jobs: it reports counts-only usage (your seats & savings), and it lets the SDK and the gateway collect your renewed license by themselves every billing period. Separate from the license key; only its hash is stored. Create one, then Test my key to confirm it's live.
installLicensePanel.shownOnce: shown once at creation — only the prefix is stored.
installLicensePanel.renewalNote: Keep this key in your deployment. Your license expires at the end of each billing period and the renewal mints a new one. With this key the SDK collects it and swaps it in without a restart. Without it nobody collects it, so someone has to paste the new key by hand every period — and if nobody does, the SDK stops once the grace period ends, even though the subscription is paid and up to date.
installLicensePanel.step3: 3 · Set it up with one command — the recommended way. Run it in your project's folder:
installLicensePanel.initNote: It reads your package.json (Next.js, Express, the Vercel AI SDK, Mastra, LangChain.js, the Anthropic SDK or the OpenAI SDK) and prints what your stack needs: the install line for your package manager, which keys are still missing, the exact code for your adapter and a check that spends no tokens — the layer answers it on your machine, without calling the model. It writes nothing: --write creates new files only, after asking you, and never overwrites an existing one.
installLicensePanel.manualInstall: Prefer to wire it by hand? Install the package — public on npm, no token, no config:
installLicensePanel.manualWire: …then wire your provider and read the SavingsReport:
installLicensePanel.gatewayNote: Coding agent instead of an app? The same package ships a local measuring gateway: bvsala claude launches Claude Code through it and this dashboard shows the spend, token by token. It uses the same service key from step 2 and collects your license by itself — like the SDK, it does not start without an active license.
installLicensePanel.doctorComment: other agents and SDKs: the exact configuration for each
installLicensePanel.agentsNote: Each wrapper sets its agent up for that session only — nothing in its configuration changes — and on exit tells you how many requests it metered, which ones it could not, and why. bvsala copilot needs your own Anthropic key (BYOK): GitHub-hosted models never go through a base URL, so there is nothing to meter. For Crush, Droid, Cline, Continue or Copilot in VS Code, bvsala doctor prints the exact configuration. Cursor cannot be metered: it sends every request, your own key included, from its own servers, which cannot reach a gateway on your machine. Gemini CLI, not yet: it speaks the Gemini API, whose usage counter the gateway does not read yet.
installLicensePanel.pythonNote: Python? The bvsala client for Python routes the official OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs through this same gateway (bvsala gateway) and hands your code the report of each request — the same figures this dashboard receives. It needs a 0.4.26 or later gateway and Python 3.10 or newer. It is not on PyPI yet: until it is, it installs from the repository with pip install ./packages/python, and the repository is not public yet — if you need it now, write to support@bivelio.com.
installLicensePanel.finalNote: That's it. No valid license → generate() refuses. If your plan is cancelled the SDK stops within ~15 min via licenseServerUrl — no restart, and it never bricks your production if we're unreachable.

tokenTotals.spentWhat: input + output, what your provider billed
tokenTotals.unavailable: token counters not available yet for this account; if you already have traffic and see this, write to support@bivelio.com
tokenTotals.footnote: Output saving is almost always zero, and that is not a bug: on a call that actually ran the layer does not shrink the answer, so its output baseline is the measured output. Token savings live in the input and in avoided calls. A NEGATIVE total is not an error either: it means the layer spent more than it would have cost without it, and we show it.

sombraElision.title: Shadow elision (hypothetical)
sombraElision.nota: What context elision would have saved on your real traffic, computed by the gateway without touching a single byte. It is never added to the headline and never enters the commission: the lever only turns on when this figure justifies it.
sombraElision.notaNegativa: On your traffic, elision would have cost money: rewriting blocks invalidates the provider's prefix cache. This lane exists precisely to see that before turning anything on — which is why it stays off.

elisionProveedor.title: Provider clearing caused by our dials
elisionProveedor.nota: The count is the provider's (applied_edits). It is not a measured saving and never enters your commission; money will follow once the net per model is measured — clearing rewrites the prefix cache, and on some models the net is negative.

ritmo.comisionCalibracion: Calibration month: nothing is charged. The figure is the commission there would be.
ritmo.cerrado: Closed period: this is what it was, not where it is heading.

extracto.eyebrow: Shadow mode · nothing is charged here
extracto.title: Your statement, before the invoice exists
extracto.intro: The exact document the future variable invoice will produce: measured savings only, with the tiered rate and no minimum — no measured savings, no commission. The seat fee is a separate, fixed monthly charge. During calibration, the commission is always {cero}.
extracto.lecturaFallo: Could not read this period's usage. The statement below may be incomplete.

extracto.notaSombra: Shadow figure: the computed commission is {comision}. No invoice includes it yet.
extracto.sinAhorro: No measured savings this period — no measured savings, no commission. Ever.
extracto.estimadoExcluido: Estimated savings excluded from the base (context, never billable): {usd}.
extracto.sombraElision: Shadow lane: elision would have saved {usd} across {requests} simulated requests. Hypothetical — it never enters the base or the commission.
extracto.sombraElisionNegativa: Shadow lane: elision would have cost an extra {usd} across {requests} simulated requests. That is why it stays off: only what truly saves gets turned on.
extracto.elisionProveedor: Provider clearing lane: {requests} requests where our dials made the provider clear context. A count, not a saving — it never enters the base or the commission.
extracto.referencia: Measured by reference: {usd} across {requests, plural, one {# repeated request} other {# repeated requests}} served without calling your provider. Each is valued with the counter your provider returned for the identical request that already ran — it is in that request's report and in your provider's usage for that day — at the cached-input rate, the lowest your provider bills for repeating a prompt; the output only counts when sampling was deterministic and the call that ran carried no hidden reasoning (your provider reported zero reasoning tokens or, where it does not break them out, its answer had no reasoning block). Included in the base.
extracto.referenciaExcluida: Measured by reference: {usd} across {requests, plural, one {# repeated request} other {# repeated requests}}. Shown for context — for now it is kept out of the base and the commission.
extracto.exportarReferencias: Download the repeated requests of this period, one row each (CSV)
extracto.exportarReferenciasPorDia: Too many repeated requests for a single file — download this period one day at a time (CSV):
extracto.parametros: Statement parameters — price catalog {version} · exchange rate {fx}.
extracto.parametrosReferencia: Rule for repeated requests ({regla}): the request that ran must be byte-identical, untouched by the layer (an output schema counts only when it traveled exactly as you sent it, in strict mode, in your provider's native response-format parameter, with nothing added to the prompt) and at most {dias} days old; input at your provider's cached-input rate; output at {cuota} of its counter, never above this request's output limit, and only with deterministic sampling, on a model in our price catalog that does not reason and honors that sampling, when the call that ran carried no hidden reasoning (your provider reported zero reasoning tokens or, where it does not break them out, its answer had no reasoning block).
extracto.mismaFacturaTitulo: This document IS the future invoice.

steps.title: Compress what remains
steps.sub: leaner encoding · only when it pays off

explica.title: What does the SDK actually do?

pasos.title: AI charges you per word
pasos.body: Every request to an AI is paid for by the text going in and out. Savings stands in the middle of that path and lets through only what's needed: whatever you didn't have to pay for drops into your jar.

pasos.title: You don't pay twice for the same thing
pasos.body: An AI re-reads everything you already sent it, turn after turn — and the provider charges for it again. Savings prepares every request so the provider applies its discounted price to the repeats. The discount is the provider's; our part is asking for it properly.

pasos.title: A receipt you can verify
pasos.body: We don't ask for faith. Every saving is measured with the provider's official meter — the same one they bill you with — and lands on your receipt. Anything that can't be checked against the bill is never announced.

pasos.title: A seat fee, and a share of what's measured
pasos.body: You pay a fixed fee per seat every month, whether or not you save. On top of it, our commission comes only out of savings measured with your provider's meter — and most of every saving always stays with you. A month with no measured savings? You pay the seats and zero commission.

explica.nota: The animations illustrate the idea. The real numbers — measured against live providers — are right below.

step2.title: How do we know it saves? We measure it — and we publish every trial, one by one.
step2.body: Every scenario runs twice against the real provider: as-is, and with Savings in front. Both results are counted with the provider's own meter — the same one that prices your bill. Here is what came out, error margin included:
step2.videoCaption: The test is a fair experiment: the same task twice — without Savings and with Savings — with the provider's own meter counting both.
step2.plain: In this test, the bill went down by at least {piso}, with near certainty. Most likely it went down by {punto}.
step2.plainSdkPendiente: With the SDK as you install it from npm, the bill goes down by at least {piso}. The published test also carried a bench-only compressor that the package does not ship; we take its effect out instead of counting it, until a run of the installed SDK replaces this figure.
step2.plainNote: When there's a range, we always announce the small number — the one statistics guarantees — never the flattering one.

ledgersHead.title: Every kind of saving, counted separately — so no number gets inflated.
ledgersHead.body: Savings saves in several ways: it avoids whole calls, removes text you didn't need, packs what's sent more tightly, and switches on the provider's discounts. Each way keeps its own ledger with its own measured figure — and we never add them up into one marketing number.
ledgersHead.providerNote: Each ledger is measured and published on its own against the OpenAI API; the ones that do not clear zero do not appear. A percentage without its model next to it means nothing: the same lever can save on one model and cost on another.

skill.title: The skill that stretches your subscription caps
skill.body: No invoice doesn't mean no pain: the five-hour window and the weekly cap. savings-mode is a pure-instructions skill — no proxy, your traffic untouched — that cuts the two masses that actually burn cap: model output and tool results. It's free; what you pay Savings for is knowing how much it saves you.
skill.mLecturaDesc: The whole context is re-read every turn — which is why keeping it lean matters.
skill.mEscrituraDesc: Every tool result is cache-written at a premium before being re-read.
skill.mSalidaDesc: Under one percent of the tokens; the skill attacks it directly.

Your AGENTS.md outside the marks is never touched. Works with ChatGPT accounts and API keys, and under bvsala codex (with a license) its effect is measured.

gateway.title: Claude Code on an API key? See its real spend, token by token.
gateway.body: One command puts a local meter in front of your terminal, with no changes to your code: export your service key and start your agent through bvsala. Your prompts never leave your machine — only counts and cost reach your dashboard.
gateway.note: The gateway measures, with your provider's own counter, every request whose usage the provider reports (for models in our price catalog) and, like the SDK, runs only with an active license: it collects it with your service key and verifies its signature on your machine. With a PRO license, on Anthropic models, it also applies one lever by default: it moves cache writes from the one-hour TTL to the five-minute one only on turns where a large part of the prompt is new — such as a session's first turn or a compaction — and leaves chained turns as they are. That changes the price, never the content the model reads. The other levers stay off until you switch them on. The savings-mode skill is available for your caps, with its effect still to be measured. The gateway also works with Codex CLI, Goose, Qwen Code, opencode, Kilo, Aider and, with your own Anthropic key, GitHub Copilot CLI; for others, such as Cline or Continue, bvsala doctor prints the exact configuration. Cursor cannot be metered, and Gemini CLI not yet.
gateway.pythonNote: Python or any other language? Point the official OpenAI or Anthropic SDK at the gateway and every request whose usage the provider reports, for a model with a list price, is recorded in this dashboard at that price; the gateway's log says when one is not. bvsala doctor prints the base URL for each SDK. For OpenAI streaming, ask for usage in the request (stream_options.include_usage).

integrate.title: Run it in your own app. Your prompts never touch our servers.
integrate.body: Drop the SDK in front of your provider. Every response carries a full SavingsReport you can chart — the same numbers the dashboard reads.
integrate.initNote: Or let one command tailor it to your stack. init reads your package.json (Next.js, Express, the Vercel AI SDK, Mastra, LangChain.js, the Anthropic or the OpenAI SDK) and prints the install line, the exact code for your adapter and a check that spends no tokens: once your license is in place, the layer answers it on your machine, without calling the model. It writes nothing unless you ask it to.

The commission is on top, and only on savings measured with your provider's meter — including repeated requests served without calling your provider, each valued with the counter of the identical request that already ran. Estimates never enter it.

devs.title: Fewer bill headaches. Without changing provider.
devs.sub: Four facts about the package. None of them is a promise.

cards.title: Zero runtime dependencies
cards.body: A single ESM bundle. Nothing gets installed next to your code that we did not write; the exact tokenizer is an optional peer.

cards.title: One SavingsReport per call
cards.body: Four ledgers that are never summed, the cost with its basis (measured or estimated) and traces per stage. It is the same thing your dashboard reads.

cards.title: Your traffic still goes direct
cards.body: The SDK wraps the call inside your process. Your prompts never pass through BiVelio: we only ever receive counts and cost.

cards.title: Streaming, same report
cards.body: generateStream() hands you the answer as the provider writes it and closes with the same SavingsReport as generate(), under the same basis rules: the provider's final counter is read at the end of the stream, and a stream without it is reported as unmeasured and never enters your commission. With an output contract, the answer arrives validated, in one piece.

offers.title: Where do your tokens go: your app, or your coding agent?
offers.sub: Both are licensed per seat and both count with your provider's own meter. They do different jobs, so each makes its own promise — and today only one of them has a published savings figure.

howItWorks.metaTitle: Where does the saving install? · BiVelio Savings Layer
howItWorks.metaDescription: BV‑SALA is a layer that installs in your application's code, where the API is called. What it can save, where it doesn't apply, and how it's truly measured.
howItWorks.title: Where does the saving install?
howItWorks.lede: BV‑SALA is not an app, not an extension, not a ChatGPT setting. It's a piece of code a developer places inside their own application, right where that application calls your provider's API. It can only save where a per-token bill exists — and can only measure it where it sees every request go by.
howItWorks.s1Title: The layer lives inside your code
howItWorks.s1Sub: The same call, with and without the layer. Traffic always travels straight from your application to the provider — BV‑SALA is not a middleman server and never sees your data from outside.
howItWorks.s1Note: That green box is an npm package inside the application's code. That's why the key question is never “what do I install?” but “who wrote the code that calls the API?” — that person is who can install it. The exceptions are a coding terminal like Claude Code and an app in any language that uses the official OpenAI or Anthropic SDK and lets you set its base URL: there the bvsala gateway sits in front without touching a line of code. That traffic is measured for models with a list price; the saving levers of the npm package do not run there, and the gateway's own apply only to Anthropic traffic, with a PRO license.
howItWorks.s2Sub: Four ways of using AI, and what BV‑SALA can do in each one.
howItWorks.caseChatSub: app or web, free or paid
howItWorks.caseChatBody: You pay a flat fee (or nothing): there is no per-token bill to reduce, and it's a closed product where nobody can place software between the app and its models. BV‑SALA's saving simply doesn't apply here — and no product can honestly promise it there.
howItWorks.caseClaudeBody: Flat subscription: no token invoice to meter — but there are caps (the five-hour window and the weekly one). That is exactly what the savings-mode skill is for: free, uploaded to claude.ai in a minute, attacking the two masses that burn cap. Its effect will be published once measured — never before.
howItWorks.caseCodeBody: On a subscription the fee is flat — but capped: the same skill installs with a single command and stretches the same weekly cap. With an API key there is a real token invoice — and the meter is already running: with your BiVelio license, “bvsala claude” launches Claude Code through the local gateway and your spend shows up in the panel, token by token, without touching a line of code. With PRO, on Anthropic models, it also moves cache writes from the one-hour TTL to the five-minute one only on turns where a large part of the prompt is new (a session's first turn, a compaction): a saving computed on your provider's own token count, never on an estimate.
howItWorks.caseAppBody: The case BV‑SALA exists for. Your app calls the API with your key, the provider bills every token, and the layer installs in three steps: package, license, and wrapping the call. From the first request it returns a SavingsReport with the saving, split into measured and estimated.
howItWorks.s3Sub: The product has two different numbers, and they shouldn't be mixed.
howItWorks.mBeforeBody: The calculator in the pricing section projects your savings from your own numbers: requests, tokens and model. It's an honest projection — that's why it carries the “estimate” tag.
howItWorks.mAfterBody: Every call returns a SavingsReport: the calls you never paid for and the net saving per request. Auditable, request by request, on your own infrastructure.

pricingPage.metaDescription: The seat fee and the commission on measured savings, published from the same constants that bill you.
pricingPage.title: Pricing terms
pricingPage.governs: This page describes how the service works today; the <license>LICENSE</license> and the <terms>BiVelio Terms</terms> govern.
pricingPage.lede: Every figure on this page is read from the code that bills you, so it changes when the price changes.

seat.title: The seat fee
seat.amount: {monthly} per seat per month, or {yearly} per seat per year, in {currency}.
seat.cycle: The seat fee is billed through Stripe for each monthly or yearly cycle of your subscription, counted from the day it starts.
seat.paidAlways: The seat fee is paid whether or not the Software produces any saving.
seat.vat: Amounts exclude VAT. Checkout asks for your billing address and, optionally, your VAT number; both are printed on your invoice.
seat.what: A seat is one machine or service identity that runs the Software, not a person. You choose how many seats your subscription covers (up to {max} at checkout), and your license covers that many.
seat.counted: Each calendar month (UTC), BiVelio counts as in use every distinct seat identifier that was active on at least {dias} different days of that month. Identities flagged as CI or ephemeral runners are not counted. Your dashboard compares that count with the seats your subscription covers.
seat.identifier: How a seat identifier is formed, and everything else the Software sends to BiVelio, is on the <privacy>privacy page</privacy>.

commission.title: The commission on measured savings
commission.only: A commission is charged only on measured savings: savings labelled {labels} in your usage records. Savings labelled {never} never carry commission.
commission.measured: A measured saving is established from your LLM provider's own usage counter for that request.
commission.reference: A reference saving, for a repeated request the Software served without calling your provider, is established from your provider's counter for the identical earlier request that did run, under the rule shown on your statement ({regla}).
commission.valued: Both are valued at the per-token prices the Software applied to that request: those of a cost model you configure, where you configure one, and otherwise your provider's list prices in the price catalogue included in the Software.
commission.flatRate: Traffic the Software identifies as a flat-rate provider subscription (a Claude or ChatGPT subscription used through the local gateway) is metered but credited no measured saving, so it carries no commission.
commission.elision: The value of input tokens your provider reports as cleared from context is recorded, but it is not part of the commission base.
commission.tiersIntro: The period's measured savings are converted to {currency} and split into marginal tiers, each charged at its own rate:
commission.ceiling: No tier's rate exceeds {max}, so before the commission is rounded to the cent you keep at least {garantia} of the period's measured savings. The seat fee is separate.
commission.fx: Measured savings are counted in US dollars and converted at the European Central Bank reference rate fetched when the period is closed; your statement shows the rate used.
commission.rounding: The commission is rounded to the nearest cent. A commission below {minimo} is not invoiced and is not carried over to another period.
commission.zero: A period with no measured savings carries no commission.
commission.calculator: To see what this means for your own traffic, try the <calc>calculator</calc> on the home page.

calibration.title: Calibration period
calibration.body: The first calendar month (UTC) in which your organization reports any usage is a calibration period, however little of that month remains. It carries no commission, and its statement still shows the commission that would have applied.

exemption.title: Exemption from the commission
exemption.body: No commission is charged for a period that BiVelio closes while your account is exempt from it. An account is exempt when BiVelio grants it an exemption and, until a payment is made on the account, when its subscription was activated with a promotional code that waives the seat fee in full for its entire term. The statement still shows the commission that would have applied.

statement.title: Statement and invoice
statement.body: The commission is calculated per calendar month (UTC). After a month ends, BiVelio closes it: your dashboard's statement for that month is sealed with the measured base, the tiers, the exchange rate and the price-catalogue version, and the commission is invoiced from that statement through Stripe, on an invoice separate from the seat fee.

privacyPage.metaDescription: The exact list of what the SDK and the local gateway send to BiVelio, what they never send, and how long BiVelio keeps it.
privacyPage.title: What leaves your infrastructure
privacyPage.governs: This page describes how the service works today; the <license>LICENSE</license> and the <terms>BiVelio Terms</terms> govern.
privacyPage.lede: What the Software (the SDK and the local gateway) sends to BiVelio, what it never sends, and how long BiVelio keeps it.

never.title: Never sent to BiVelio
never.content: The content of your requests and responses: prompts, system instructions, messages, tool definitions, tool arguments and results, retrieved documents, and completions.
never.credentials: The credentials you use with your LLM provider: API keys, OAuth tokens, or other authorization headers.
never.path: That content and those credentials travel only between your systems and the LLM provider you configure.

usage.title: Usage records
usage.when: The SDK sends usage records only when you configure a license server or metering URL; the local gateway always does. Each batch carries your BiVelio service-account key, which identifies your organization, and the Software's surface and version in the {header} header.
usage.limit: Each record is limited to the fields below. BiVelio's ingest rejects any record that carries a field not on this list.

ids.title: Identifiers
ids.body: A request identifier generated on your side (at random, or by your own generator). For a repeated request valued by reference, the identifier and time of the earlier request whose provider counter is used. A seat identifier: a value you set, or an opaque value computed on your machine as a keyed hash (HMAC), keyed with your service-account key, of the platform, CPU architecture, runtime executable path, host name, operating-system user name and home directory; those underlying values are never sent. Through the local gateway, the session and sub-agent identifiers your coding agent attaches to its own requests (for example, Claude Code's session id), only when they are plain identifiers. An organization hint (BiVelio always derives your organization from the key). A flag marking CI or ephemeral runners.

model.title: Model and time
model.body: The identifier of the model that served the request: the model named in the request or, where the Software sent the request to another model under a setting you enabled, that model; for a self-hosted or Azure deployment, the name you gave it. And the time of the request.

counts.title: Counts
counts.body: LLM calls executed and avoided; input and output tokens before and after the Software's optimizations, including tokens removed, compressed, or read from the provider's cache; and the cache outcome.

cost.title: Cost
cost.body: Cost figures computed by the Software from its price catalogue, or from a cost model you supply: baseline cost, actual cost, the net-saving ratio, the basis of the figures (measured, reference, estimated, shadow or unmeasured), and the value, at the provider's cache-read price, of input tokens your provider reported as cleared from context.

verification.title: Optional verification (SDK only, off by default)
verification.when: If you turn on the SDK's verification option, the SDK sends a sample of the requests it served to your own provider again, without optimization, and discards that second response. For each sampled request it sends BiVelio, through a separate channel, only the fields below; that channel also rejects any other field, and nothing it receives is used to calculate the commission.

sample.title: Each sampled request
sample.body: The label verification, the request identifier and time; the model requested and the model that served; the cache outcome; the category of the request and the outcome of the check; the input, cached-input and output tokens and the cost of the served request and of the unoptimized copy; how the copy finished and whether it met the response contract; and the per-token prices applied.

counts.title: Daily counts
counts.body: For each day, the number of requests in each category, including the requests excluded from the check.

batch.title: Each batch
batch.body: A random batch identifier, used to discard duplicates, and the two lists above.

other.title: Other requests to BiVelio
other.body: The Software also fetches its current license token and the signed license revocation list, and the local gateway fetches your organization's feature entitlements. These requests carry your service-account key where authentication is required, and no request data.
other.network: Like any HTTPS request, all of the above also reveals ordinary network metadata, such as your IP address.

retention.title: What BiVelio keeps, and for how long
retention.intro: The ingest adds each usage record to daily totals: per day, per model, per seat and per gateway session. Individual rows are kept only in the places below, and a daily job deletes each row once it is older than its period:

items.seen: Request identifiers, kept to discard duplicate records: {dias} days.
items.reference: Repeated requests valued by reference (request identifiers, model, time and the provider counter used), the rows behind your statement's download: {dias} days.
items.verificationSamples: Verification samples and their daily counts: {dias} days.

retention.noSchedule: Daily totals, seat activity and your sealed statements have no automatic deletion schedule today.

use.title: What BiVelio uses it for
use.body: To operate licensing and revocation, show your dashboard, count seats in use, and calculate the fees described on the <pricing>pricing page</pricing>.

account.title: Your account on this website
account.body: Your sign-in e-mail, your organization and your billing details (payments are processed by Stripe) are covered by <policy>BiVelio's privacy policy</policy>.

privacyPage.contact: Questions and requests about this data: <mail>{email}</mail>.
